Insight pointers

Data-backed speaking points for the brand team. Counts refer to the uploaded serum KYC sheet.

01

Glow is the strongest shared thread

Dullness/lack of glow is the most common purchase motivation (6 mentions); more glow/radiance is the leading desired outcome (8), and more glow is the leading reported result (9).

Keep glow/radiance as a lead benefit, but distinguish the desired outcome from the result consumers say they noticed.
Consumer wording: “This brought some brightness back.”
02

Visible results coexist with a meaningful slow-results problem

Eight mentions describe slight improvement and three record no noticeable difference; comments also repeatedly describe outcomes as slow or mild.

Set realistic timelines and explain what kind of change users should look for, without implying every consumer sees the same result.
Consumer wording: “Tried for 6 weeks. Skin same as before.”
03

Choice is not driven by claims alone

Existing use of The Derma Co. products and friend/family recommendations each appear 5 times; brand reputation and price appear 3 times each.

Support product claims with accessible proof while maintaining referral and cross-product familiarity cues.
Consumer wording: “Recommended by friend / family.”
04

Repurchase intent is positive but not settled

15 of 24 answered repurchase questions are definitely/probably yes; 5 are maybe and 4 probably no.

Understand the barrier behind maybe/no responses, especially slow results, mild efficacy and reported irritation.
Consumer wording: “Maybe, results slow.”
05

Competitor pressure is mixed with first-serum adoption

Some mention Cetaphil, Cureskin or Minimalist, while several answers describe a first serum or no prior serum.

Separate conversion from an established competitor from onboarding a new serum user; these require different communication.
Consumer wording: “First serum ever.”
06

Brand associations are fragmented

Science-based and cheap are the only associations repeated twice as standalone answers; most brand-word combinations occur once.

Do not assume one dominant brand meaning from this sample; validate whether clinical credibility and value are consistently understood.
Consumer wording: “Science-based.”
